caption: A paint roller, dipped in green paint, is used to cover a section of a metal fence, creating a uniform green coat.
scope: Eight predeclared frames; qualitative process/identity assessment, not an aggregate score
observations: A new handheld roller appears while the original horizontal roller-like object remains on the fence; this creates a potential duplicate-tool/role-consistency defect.

The new roller is relatively coherent as it moves, but preserving its geometry does not resolve the duplicated original object. The initial fence is already green, so a visible new uniform coat is difficult to verify from these frames.
Without fusion, the original roller leaves the fence and becomes the moving tool, avoiding the fixed-original plus second-roller pattern in normal output.
The no_c tool support and handle deform and change shape during this transition, and the exposed patch changes abruptly; disabling physics is not a clean correct solution either.
Normal stabilizes the new tool geometry but retains a duplicate original role. A physical-stability benefit alone does not establish semantic or visual success.
